report.previous_run_delta: Fresh: Browser Run crawl jobs can now push lifecycle events into Queues; static render:false crawls remain unbilled during beta. Fresh strengthening: Vercel Sandbox exposes memory usage, thresholds, queries, and alerts. Closing today: Jev and Ling Flash Fin free windows. signals.signal_type: FRESH EVENT-DRIVEN RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE / TEMPORARILY UNBILLED BETA
signals.classification: CONFIRMED FRESH CAPABILITY; BETA ECONOMICS; NOT INDEPENDENTLY EXERCISED
signals.changed: Browser Run crawl jobs can now publish crawl.started, crawl.updated, and crawl.finished events directly to Cloudflare Queues, replacing status polling. The crawl API can fetch static HTML or Markdown with render:false, which Cloudflare says is not billed during beta.
signals.free_value: Static render:false crawling is unbilled during beta. Workers Free includes 10,000 Queue operations daily. If JavaScript rendering is required, Workers Free includes 10 Browser Run minutes daily.
signals.approximate_value: No defensible cash equivalent. It can replace polling logic and part of the manual discovery/recheck workload for LEVERAGE SEEKER while providing structured completion events.
signals.cash_required: $0 within beta static-crawl behavior and Workers Free Queue limits.
signals.eligibility_reality_check: Requires a Cloudflare account, Browser Rendering Edit API token, a Queue and consumer. Events are account-wide for all crawl jobs. Crawls respect robots.txt, Content Signals, crawl delays, bot protection, CAPTCHAs, and target-site restrictions.
signals.why_asymmetric: A daily scout can submit narrow vendor changelog or program-page crawls, sleep without polling, then trigger comparison and ICE processing only when a job finishes.

evidence.confirmed_fact: Cloudflare documents lifecycle subscriptions, push delivery through Queues, static render:false crawling without beta billing, 10,000 daily Free Queue operations, result retention, and crawl restrictions.
evidence.inference: This could become a low-cost event source for LEVERAGE SEEKER program and launch reconciliation.
evidence.unverified_claim: End-to-end reliability, duplicate-event handling, extraction fidelity, and savings versus the current scout were not measured.

signals.catch: Lifecycle events contain status, not page content; the consumer must fetch results after completion. Results expire after 14 days, jobs time out after seven days, event subscriptions cover every crawl in the account, and render:false will eventually move to ordinary Workers billing.
signals.window: Event subscriptions launched September 25. Static render:false crawling is unbilled only during an undated beta.
signals.immediate_exploit: Crawl one public vendor changelog with render:false, limit 20, Markdown output, narrow include patterns, and declared reference/ai-input purposes. Route completion to a Queue, fetch the result once, hash it, and compare it with the previous snapshot.

signals.classification: CONFIRMED FRESH CAPABILITY; FREE FAIL-CLOSED HOBBY TEST
signals.changed: Sandbox dashboards and the vercel metrics CLI now expose memory usage. Charts include average, P75 and P95, an 85% memory-ceiling reference line, custom-query support, and alert creation.
signals.free_value: Hobby includes 5 active CPU hours, 420 GB-hours of provisioned memory, 5,000 creations, 20 GB transfer, 15 GB snapshots, and fail-closed quota behavior. No separate memory-observability fee is published.
signals.approximate_value: Unquantified. It replaces custom memory telemetry and gives B2ROOT evidence for right-sizing or terminating resource-heavy agent sandboxes.
signals.cash_required: $0 within Hobby quotas; Sandbox creation pauses rather than billing when Hobby limits are exceeded.
signals.eligibility_reality_check: Requires a Vercel account, Sandbox workload, and linked project for CLI metrics. No company, funding, incorporation, geography, card, or partner gate is published for Hobby use.
signals.why_asymmetric: The persistent workspace and snapshot stack reported September 22 now gains a measurable resource boundary, allowing resume experiments to capture memory cost and alert before failure.

evidence.confirmed_fact: Vercel documents dashboard and CLI metrics, average/P75/P95 views, an 85% limit line, custom queries, alerts, Hobby quotas, and pause-not-charge behavior.
evidence.inference: Memory evidence can become part of B2ROOT trajectory cost and environment manifests.
evidence.unverified_claim: Metric latency, alert delivery, and usefulness for detecting the user’s prior inference runaway were not tested.

signals.catch: Memory observability does not measure model-token spend and cannot stop inference loops by itself. Provisioned memory is a billing dimension on paid plans; alerts are evidence, not enforcement unless coupled to termination policy.
signals.immediate_exploit: Run one known small Sandbox task, deliberately approach but do not exceed 85% memory, record CLI and dashboard readings, and verify Hobby pause behavior remains fail-closed.

program_surface_results: No new bootstrapped-accessible magnitude program cleared verification.

Vercel advertises up to $30,000, but the application requires an approved startup partner, proof from the partner portal, Series A or earlier status, and application within 12 months of funding. It is excluded for the current bootstrapped profile despite the headline.
The 60–90-day lookback found no additional still-actionable Devin-class opportunity absent from the ledger.
